blocks.text:
Explanation:- The meaning of “Ribat” is “to camp at the border of an Islamic land to guard it from enemies. This is the well-known meaning of the word Ribat. It is a very great deed. Just as one stays with the army at the frontier and engages in guarding it, through these deeds one protects oneself from the attacks of the Nafs and Shaytan; perhaps that is why the Prophet ﷺ called these deeds “Ribat' in the above hadith.
(Mirqat)

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ عَامِرٍ ﵁ يُحَدِّثُ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: إِذَا تَطَهَّرَ الرَّجُلُ ثُمَّ أَتَي الْمَسْجِدَ يَرْعَي الصَّلَاةَ كَتَبَ لَهُ كَاتِبَاهُ أَوْكَاتِبُهُ بِكُلِّ خُطْوَةٍ يَخْطُوهَا إِلَي الْمَسْجِدِ عَشَرَ حَسَنَاتٍ، وَالْقَاعِدُ يَرْعَي الصَّلَاةَ كَالْقَانِتِ، وَيُكْتَبُ مِنَ الْمُصَلِّينَ مِنْ حِينَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ حَتَّي يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْهِ.
blocks.tamil_translation: “Whoever makes Wudu well, comes to the masjid and waits for the Salah, the angels who write his deeds write ten good deeds for every step he takes towards the masjid. The one waiting for Salah is counted as one engaged in Ibadah, and from the time he sets out from his home until he returns home he is counted among those praying,” Hazrat Uqbah ibn Amir (RA) narrates that Rasulullah ﷺ said

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ مُعَاذِ بْنِ جَبَلٍ ﵁ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِيمَا يَرْوِي عَنْ رَبِّهِ قَالَ اللهُ تَعَالَي: يَا مُحَمَّدُ! قُلْتُ: لَبَّيْكَ رَبِّ، قَالَ: فِيمَ يَخْتَصِمُ الْمَلأُ الأَعْلَي؟ قُلْتُ: فِي الْكَفَّارَاتِ، قَالَ: مَاهُنَّ؟ قُلْتُ: مَشْيُ اْلاَقْدَامِ
